History:
- Chief complaint: New-onset headache.
- Onset/duration: Began yesterday mid-morning; present ~1 day.
- Location/quality: Left posterior scalp; throbbing; intensity 8/10.
- Course: Gradually built up; no clear diurnal variation; unchanged by position, coughing, bending.
- Associated symptoms: No nausea, vomiting, visual changes, photophobia, limb weakness, numbness, fever, chills, rash, neck stiffness.
- Triggers/precipitants: None identified; no recent stress, dietary, or lifestyle changes.
- Previous episodes: None reported.
- Impact: Difficulty concentrating on work; has not missed work.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Denies any.
- Surgical/hospital history: Not discussed.
- Allergies: Denies known drug or food allergies.
- Medications: None routinely. Took Ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Family history: Mother – hypertension and migraines.
- Social: Non-smoker, no alcohol or recreational drug use. Lives with partner. Occupation – designer.

Physical Examination:
(Teleconsultation ‑ limited)
- General: Alert, conversing normally.
- Appearance: No reported rash or distress.
- Neurologic: Denies focal weakness, numbness, tingling.
- HEENT: Denies visual disturbance, photophobia, eye pain.
- No fever, chills, vomiting reported.
(Note: No vitals or in-person exam performed.)

Impression:
New-onset unilateral throbbing headache, likely primary (probable tension-type vs first migraine); no current red-flag features.

Management Plan:
- Prescribed/arranged stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) to be taken with food, in place of Ibuprofen.
- May use Paracetamol concurrently for additional analgesia.
- Advise good rest and adequate hydration.
- Red-flag advice: Seek medical review if headache worsens, persists beyond 1–2 days, or if fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or recurrent similar episodes develop.
- Follow-up: Phone consultation if not improving after trial of medication within 1–2 days.

Patient Summary:
28-year-old woman with first episode of severe left-sided throbbing headache without associated neurological or systemic symptoms. No prior headache history. Empiric analgesia and safety-net advice provided; plan to reassess if not resolving.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed alternative NSAID with meals; may add Paracetamol.
- Maintain hydration and rest.
- Contact provider or seek urgent care if pain worsens, lasts >48 h, or any new concerning symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness).

Next Steps:
- Monitor response over next 1–2 days.
- Re-evaluate (tele-visit or in-person) if inadequate improvement or development of red-flag features.
- Consider BP measurement and further headache work-up if symptoms persist or recur.

● Missing expected elements: Objective vitals (BP, HR, temperature), full neurological exam, allergy verification beyond patient’s statement, detailed medication name/dose, past surgical history.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
